answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The harbor multiplier is published, charged in meadow, and karst lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3635 identities would post 1680 proofs and burn roughly 67 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
